title: Pinned session escape and quarantine policy for canary/A-B rollouts
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Problem: When version pinning and session affinity are used during canary or A-B rollouts, pinned sessions can become a vector for prolonged exposure to a bad variant (regressions, capacity exhaustion, or regional perf issues). We need a deterministic, operator-observable policy that allows a pinned session to 'escape' to a healthy variant under defined conditions, with a quarantine/escrow mechanism to avoid thrashing and to preserve reproducibility for debugging. Goal: define escape triggers, grace windows, probabilistic vs deterministic escapes, quarantine duration and behavior, metrics to surface, and an implementable runtime algorithm that integrates with the existing routing resolver and pin TTL machinery.
acceptance_criteria: A clear, unambiguous specification of escape triggers (capacity, error-rate, latency SLO breach, health probe failures, model quality regression)
Design includes both deterministic and probabilistic escape modes and when each should be used
Specified quarantine behavior: how long a session remains quarantined, whether it can be re-pinned, and how to surface quarantined sessions in the Console
Runtime contract: updated routing resolver algorithm pseudocode + complexity/latency budget and fallbacks when resolver cannot be reached
E2E test plan and load test scenarios that demonstrate correct escape behavior under capacity and quality regressions
Dashboard and alert specs for operators (percent of pinned sessions escaped, quarantine pool size, escaped-by-trigger breakdown)
PR with prototype implementation and integration tests merged into feature branch with accompanying rollout plan
design_decisions: Escape triggers will be tiered: immediate deterministic triggers (hard errors, node OOM, model crash), soft triggers (p95 latency > threshold, error-rate spike) subject to grace window, and quality triggers (eval regression) handled via controlled decay

Pinned sessions carry a small, server-side mutable token: anchor_state={pinned_version, pin_ttl, quarantine_until, escape_history_hash} — this token is opaque to clients and stored with minimal metadata in routing state store
Deterministic escape uses a hard swap to the primary fallback variant for that session; probabilistic escape uses weighted rewrites to move a session with X% probability per request until migrated

Quarantine is a short-lived isolate pool per-region+tier+version. Quarantined sessions route to a neutral fallback (stable variant) while flagged for post-mortem analysis. Quarantine TTL default is 5 minutes, configurable per-release
Operators can opt into two modes at rollout start: conservative (probabilistic escape + long quarantine) or aggressive (deterministic escape + short quarantine) depending on customer-impact and SLAs
Routing resolver will expose monotonic escape counters to avoid repeated oscillations; a session can be escaped at most N times in M minutes (defaults: N=2, M=30)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec and lightweight actor in routing resolver to evaluate local health signals and publish escape decisions (2 weeks)
Phase 2: KV-backed anchor token store migration and small schema addition to request metadata (feature branch) (1 week)
Phase 3: Implement deterministic and probabilistic escape code paths in runtime with feature flag gating and integration tests (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Console surface for quarantined sessions + alerting + runbook (1 week)
Phase 5: Canary rollout of feature behind customer flag, A/B test with synthetic traffic and chaos for failures (2 weeks)
Owners: Ava (runtime), Priya (observability), Jonas (routing resolver), Marcus (release orchestration)
testing_plan: Unit tests for anchor token transitions (pin -> escape -> quarantine -> re-pin) with boundary conditions
Integration tests that simulate node OOM/failure and verify deterministic escape to fallback without session loss
Load tests that create pinned-hot sessions and then exhaust capacity on canary; assert that escape reduces pressure within the SLA window
Quality regression test: inject degraded outputs for canary variant and verify controlled probabilistic decay of pin affinity and operator-visible logs
Chaos test: intermittent control-plane partition to verify conservative fallback when routing resolver unreachable
rollout_plan: Gate 0: feature flag off in prod clusters; internal dev cluster testing
Gate 1: enable in non-critical region with synthetic traffic and narrow-canary customers
Gate 2: progressive enable behind conservative mode for 25% of rollouts by weight, monitor escape metrics for 48h
Gate 3: enable aggressive mode for new rollouts if metrics stable for 7 days
Rollback: immediate global disable of escape mechanics via control-plane feature flag; automatic revert of quarantined sessions back to previous pinned version if needed
monitoring_and_ops: Console panels: escaped_sessions_rate, quarantine_pool_size, escapes_by_trigger (capacity|errors|quality|latency), rebind_success_rate
Alerts: high escape rate (>2% of pinned sessions in 10m) or large quarantine (>500 sessions in region) triggers on-call with severity mapping
Log context: each escape event must include session_id, original_version, target_variant, trigger_type, timestamp, node_id
Runbook: step-by-step for operators to inspect quarantined sessions, re-pin safe sessions, and perform manual graduation
Post-mortem checklist: correlate escapes with deployment events, model pushes, infra incidents
